questions.correct_answer: Unlike related phenomena, Stille Coupling specifically denotes: A palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction between an organotin reagent (R-SnR'₃) and an organic halide or triflate.
questions.explanation: Concept discrimination: Stille Coupling is uniquely defined by: 'A palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction between an organotin reagent (R-SnR'₃) and an organic halide or triflate.'. The alternative statements erroneously attribute principles of 'Negishi Coupling', 'Oxidative Addition', or 'Alkene Metathesis' to 'Stille Coupling'.

questions.question: Which statement best discriminates 'Negishi Coupling' from other related principles in Introduction to Organometallic Compounds?

options.label: A
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Negishi Coupling is properly defined as: A chemical compound containing at least one direct covalent or polar covalent bond between a carbon atom and a metal atom (C-M).

options.label: B
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Negishi Coupling is properly defined as: A stereospecific cyclopropanation of alkenes using diiodomethane (CH₂I₂) and a zinc-copper couple (Zn(Cu)) generating a transient zinc carbenoid.

options.label: C
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Negishi Coupling is properly defined as: A lithium dialkylcuprate reagent (R₂CuLi) used for selective 1,4-conjugate additions to enones and carbon-carbon cross-coupling reactions.
